四级核心词汇 · 15英文原文

The Name at the Bottom of the List

名单最下面的那个名字 · 594 词 · 7 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A textile plant had lost its largest contract during an economic crisis. Its annual budget showed a considerable deficit, and its debt was growing. The manager planned to sell an idle workshop. An older worker, Ben, wanted the plant to use that asset to train apprentices. He knew how to weave a strong cloth on an old machine. He would soon retire on a modest pension. A new bid depended on skill. If he left, the plant might lose a valuable prospect.

2The manager asked for a feasible plan. Ben proposed a joint venture with a technical college. The college could fund the first course. The plant could insure the equipment, provide the facility, and pay a fair rate for each hour of labor. The manager wanted to recruit only people who could start at an intermediate level. Ben asked how anyone could demonstrate aptitude if regulations prohibited touching a machine.

3The college opened registration. Rina, a migrant worker, wrote her name at the bottom of the list. She could sew a straight seam. Prejudice against workers with her background had kept her away from the plant's controls. The conventional test asked for a comprehensive written account of how to operate a loom. She did not know the appropriate terms on its modern controls. Ben asked the college to evaluate her with an oral test and a practical task. Her performance showed she was capable of learning the controls.

4The teacher made safety training compulsory. The written test was optional unless an employer required it. He asked every applicant to identify the emergency switch. One recruit wore a loose sleeve that could interfere with a moving part. Ben showed him how to secure it. The insurance adviser insisted they install guards at each station and equip workers with goggles. Both sides agreed that protecting a worker was more important than keeping the training brief.

5The first group could now enroll in a four-week intensive course. Ben had expected the recruits to imitate him. Rina had a different approach. She placed a pad under a noisy support and recorded how the machine responded. The cloth came out more evenly. The manager hoped to initiate modifications at once. Rina asked for a second trial before they invested a substantial sum. The new support might improve one machine and make another less stable.

6The test showed that only two supports needed work. Their replacement enabled the plant to accept a smaller order with stricter quality rules. The manager used the revenue to supplement the training fund. He still needed to tackle the budget deficit, but there was a tangible result. The plant could maintain production. The college could fulfill its promise to give pupils a place to apply their skills. The college agreed to facilitate visits by other workshops, provided the plant could ensure that trainees had time to practice. Ben said industrializing a small craft could create jobs and still destroy an invaluable skill. Their strategy was to evaluate the outcome by the quality of the cloth and by whether a new worker could teach the process to somebody else.

7When the course ended, Ben was asked which improvement had mattered most. He pointed to the registration sheet. He had thought expertise meant working a machine well. It also meant recognizing who might learn to work it better. Rina registered for an advanced course and volunteered to help the next group. A name at the bottom of a list had become the first one the manager called when he needed someone to explain the new process.

四级核心词汇 · 15中文译文

名单最下面的那个名字

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1经济危机期间，一家纺织厂失去了最大的合同。年度预算出现了不小的赤字，欠的债也越来越多。经理打算卖掉一间闲置车间。老工人本想让工厂用这项资产带学徒。他知道怎样用一台老机器织出结实的布，自己却快要退休，往后靠一份不算多的养老金生活。新订单能不能争取到，靠的是手艺。等他一走，工厂可能也会失去一个有价值的机会。

2经理要他提出一个可行的方案。本建议和技术学院合办项目，由学院出钱开第一期课。工厂可以给设备投保，提供场地，再按合理的时薪支付劳动报酬。经理只想招一上来就达到中级水平的人。本问，如果规定连机器都不能碰，一个人怎么能表现出有没有这方面的天分？

3学院开放报名。外来务工者丽娜把自己的名字写在名单最下面。她能缝出笔直的接缝，但对她这种背景的工人存在偏见，她一直没机会操作厂里的机器。旧考试要求用文字全面说明怎样操作织机。丽娜不认识新控制面板上的用语。本请学院用口试和实际操作来评价她。她的表现说明，她有能力学会使用那些控制装置。

4老师把安全培训定为必修。除非用人单位要求，笔试就可以自选。他请每位报名者找出紧急开关。一名学徒的袖子太松，可能妨碍活动部件。本教他把袖口扎紧。保险顾问坚持在每个工位装上防护罩，给工人发护目镜。双方都认为，保护好工人比少花点时间培训更重要。

5第一批人现在可以报名参加四周的强化课程。本原以为学徒们会照着他的做法学，丽娜却有自己的思路。她在一个会响的支座下垫了块垫子，记下机器的反应，织出来的布也更均匀了。经理想马上开始改机器。丽娜请他在投一大笔钱之前再试一次。新支座也许能让一台机器变好，却让另一台变得不稳。

6试验发现，只有两个支座需要处理。换掉它们后，工厂接下了一笔规模较小、质量要求却更高的订单。经理用收入补充培训经费。预算赤字仍要处理，但已经有了看得见的结果。工厂能维持生产，学院也能兑现给学生提供实操场地的承诺。只要厂里保证学徒有练习时间，学院就能帮忙安排其他工坊来参观。本说，把小手艺搬进工业生产能创造工作机会，也可能让一门宝贵手艺消失。他们决定用布料的品质来检验成果，也要看新工人能不能把这套做法教给别人。

7课程结束后，有人问本，哪项改进最重要。他指了指报名表。以前他觉得，专长就是自己把机器开好。现在他觉得，还要看得出谁能学着把机器开得更好。丽娜报名参加进阶课程，并自愿帮助下一批学徒。原先写在名单最下面的名字，如今成了经理需要有人解释新流程时第一个想到的名字。
